scope: Independent source-family recommendations; root owns shared coverage ledger and exact-commit combined verification.
coverage_fraction_reason: Endpoint counts are not a paper coverage percentage.

claims.title: Finite interval gARG
claims.added_evidence: Every valid generated finite prefix has an acyclic interval-gARG projection with a unique local parent. Full raw lineage identities remain in the richer record.
claims.remaining_obligation: No additional foundation gap. Endpoint gARG projection can forget raw lineage identity and breakpoint information; do not identify it with the full record.

claims.title: Genome bounds, dates, owners and metadata
claims.added_evidence: The generated history has bounded nonempty inherited intervals and physical dates with strict chronology. Owner projection is treated explicitly and conditionally.
claims.remaining_obligation: Arbitrary metadata, inference of organism owners from an ARG, and a biological pedigree sampling model remain outside these results.

claims.title: Multiple crossovers and gene conversion
claims.added_evidence: No continuation theorem closes an additional obligation in this family.
claims.remaining_obligation: Encode a finite partition with a selected parent per cell; prove routing equivalence; instantiate two-cut gene conversion and multiple crossovers.

claims.title: Classical event arity and parent ordering
claims.added_evidence: The actual recorder consumes/allocates one/two lineage identities at a split and two/one at a merger. Terminal-root and one-sample boundary cases are explicit.
claims.remaining_obligation: Old endpoint-node degree theorems still require their stated ClassicalShape hypotheses. They do not become unrestricted edge-multiplicity degree decoders.

claims.title: Lossless event encoding before simplification
claims.added_evidence: Raw uncoalesced single-event records decode without the old Normalized restriction, including two distinct lineages with the same endpoints. Stable IDs and event logs retain the full generated record.
claims.remaining_obligation: The older normalized theorem remains scoped to its old representation. The new result covers the specified single-crossover event records and generated history; arbitrary multi-crossover/gene-conversion events remain M03.

claims.title: Sample-support restriction
claims.added_evidence: No continuation theorem closes an additional obligation in this family.
claims.remaining_obligation: Preserve the exact operation name. It keeps ancestors above local MRCAs, unlike M07.

claims.title: Fig.3 local-MRCA truncation
claims.added_evidence: No continuation theorem closes an additional obligation in this family.
claims.remaining_obligation: The deterministic stopping semantics is closed. Literal Figure 3 data and stochastic sample-set/count transition semantics are not supplied; B01-B06 remain separate.

claims.title: Tables and incremental local-tree recovery
claims.added_evidence: No continuation theorem closes an additional obligation in this family.
claims.remaining_obligation: Define executable sorted tables and across-coordinate remove/insert updates, prove equivalence to direct extraction and analyze record scanning, functional-cache evaluation, actual array allocation and machine costs. The new per-coordinate abstract count theorem does not prove those costs.

claims.title: Unresolved event order in coarse topology

claims.remaining_obligation: Define valid refinements and observation fibres; construct different event orders with one coarse gARG.

claims.remaining_obligation: The source broader empirical/statistical detectability discussion is not a quantified identification theorem. No detection probability or species classifier is proved.

claims.title: Big-ARG generator and event recording
claims.added_evidence: The general-n marked construction now has stable lineage IDs, full-genome splits, merger pairs, event logs, Borel-measurable finite records, a probability law, an actual-recorder adaptive mark law, and a dated-history count/time projection.
claims.remaining_obligation: Checked for positive finite sample size, positive genome length, and the declared rate normalization. Breakpoints use normalized Lebesgue measure on (0,L). Figure A1 and Little use discrete links; the Big paragraph does not explicitly switch domains. Discrete-link equivalence, an all-history real-time Markov/generator theorem, and other demographic models are not proved.

claims.title: Big nonexplosion and almost-sure absorption
claims.added_evidence: Finite jump absorption and finite physical time are transferred to the actual valid marked graph; dated histories become constant after the stopping index.
claims.remaining_obligation: The stopping rule is one active lineage (GMRCA), with n=1 stopped immediately. The final dated-validity endpoint is an almost-everywhere input-space realization theorem; do not silently rename it an output-space predicate theorem. A general unstopped CTMC construction is a stronger unproved extension.
